# DragArea

Header: `winui/ui/hosting/DragArea.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/hosting/DragArea.hpp`.

A wrapper whose content the window can be dragged by. It stands in for the caption of a borderless window, or of content extended into the title bar, where a [TitleBar](title-bar.md#uititlebar) doesn't fit, such as a splash screen's whole face, a sidebar header or a custom toolbar strip.

A press on the area moves the window, a double-click maximizes it and a right-click opens the system menu, except over a focusable control inside it: a label or icon drags, a button still clicks. In a window with an ordinary frame it does nothing. Otherwise it passes everything through to its content as [ContentHost](content-host.md#uicontenthost) does, so wrapping a subtree changes nothing about how it lays out or behaves.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::Text> label;
ui::Control<ui::Button> cancel;
window.set_content(ui::DragArea{
    .content = ui::VerticalStack{
        .content = {
            ui::Text{.text = "Loading...", .control = label},
            ui::Button{.text = "Cancel", .on_click = [] { /* ... */ }, .control = cancel},
        },
    },
});
// window.hit_region_at(label->bounds().center())  == ui::HitRegion::Caption
// window.hit_region_at(cancel->bounds().center()) == ui::HitRegion::Client
```

## `ui::DragArea`

Content the window can be dragged by, the caption stand-in for a borderless window wherever a [TitleBar](title-bar.md#uititlebar) is not the right shape. Builds a [ui::DragAreaControl](#uidragareacontrol).

Empty parts of the area hit-test as the window caption; interactive descendants (buttons, text boxes) stay ordinary client area, so they still take clicks.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::DragArea{
    .content = ui::VerticalStack{.spacing = 12, .content = {
        ui::Text{.text = "Loading..."},                                  // drags the window
        ui::Button{.text = "Cancel", .on_click = [&] { window.close(); }}, // still clickable
    }},
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::DragArea{
    .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height,
    .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uidragarea-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uidragarea-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uidragarea-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uidragarea-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uidragarea-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uidragarea-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uidragarea-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::DragArea>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |
| <span id="uidragarea-content"></span>`content` | `ui::Spec` |  | What the area shows; may be empty for a bare drag band. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::DragAreaControl](#uidragareacontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::DragAreaControl`

Derives from `ui::ContentHost`.

### hit_test_transparent

```cpp
bool hit_test_transparent() const override
```

False: the whole area takes the pointer, empty parts included, since they drag the window.

### DragAreaControl

```cpp
DragAreaControl() = default
```

An empty area; give it content with [ContentHost::set_child()](content-host.md#set_child).

### hit_region

```cpp
HitRegion hit_region(Point p) const override
```

Caption everywhere inside the area, except Client along the path under `p` from the first focusable element down (that element takes the press).
